title: Function Types

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Function Types** as part of **Functions and Parameters**. Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions. Use the subtopics—Representing Functions as Values, Function Type Signatures, Nullable Function Types—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it

items.title: Representing Functions as Values
items.text: Representing Functions as Values describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Function Type Signatures
items.text: Function Type Signatures describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Nullable Function Types
items.text: Nullable Function Types is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.
